html:
The Vargas tragedy was a series of floods and mudslides on the Caribbean coast of Venezuela, north of Caracas, in December 1999. Thousands of people died, with estimates ranging from about 10,000 to 30,000.

After days of heavy rain, the steep slopes of the coastal mountain range gave way. Torrents of mud and boulders swept down the river valleys into the towns of Vargas state, burying whole neighbourhoods built on the alluvial fans. Many bodies were never found.

It was the deadliest natural disaster in Venezuela since the earthquake of 1812. It struck in the first year of the government of Hugo Chávez, which turned down some American help. The coast was slowly rebuilt, but the disaster showed the danger of building on the slopes around Caracas.
